I see no reason at all for a community that *supposedly* prides itself on free expression and not stifling the opinions of others to have a mechanism in place that hides comments based on how many people click the "disagree" button.

Yes, in an ideal world, this mechanism would only affect spammers or other people who are poisoning the site, but in reality, where people up and downvote based on their feelings and **not** the actual content of the post, that mechanism ends up punishing anyone who dares speak against the majority, which is one of the core things that lead to Reddit's downward spiral. People are afraid to speak what they *really* feel because of the very likely chance someone or several people will get butthurt about it and downvote them into oblivion, sometimes to the point where they literally can't comment at all. That's pretty much the opposite of free expression. If you don't believe it, look at the anon subs. People express themselves much more honestly because there's *actually* no fear of repercussions, unlike on the rest of the site. Sure, you might not get banned like on Reddit, but is being silenced and ostracized because you happen to disagree with the rabid masses any better?

I also think it would make sense to put a maximum cap on the amount of downvotes a comment can receive, especially if you insist on keeping the mechanism to disallow commenting to stay in place. There's literally no reason to allow a post to gather more than 10 downvotes than it has upvotes. At that point, the community has made their feelings very clear and there's no reason to punish the person even more. Allowing unlimited downvotes encourages dogpiling. People see a comment with lots of downvotes and it affects their perception of the comment whether they want to admit it or not, and most of time it encourages them to join in on the downvote party and continue to punish the user who left the comment, forcing them to either watch their CCP plummet or delete the comment and then be berated for not standing by his word.

Basically, I think we should work a little harder on reducing some of the circlejerk on this site. It's a slippery slope and it doesn't take long for a community like this to go full-on echo chamber like Reddit did.
